parsed.study_design: Comparative cross-sectional farmer survey with before-and-after retrospective analysis and administrative data
parsed.population_and_sample: Fifty-nine peri-urban farmers in Magaral Panchayat near Chennai surveyed in 2003: all 32 farmers selling groundwater to the Water Board and 27 randomly selected non-selling farmers; administrative data also describe Chennai's water-supply system and consumers.
parsed.exposure: Participation in, or dependence on participants in, the CMWSSB–TNEB–farmer tripartite groundwater-purchasing agreement introduced in 2000.
parsed.outcome: Water availability and exclusion among farmers, cultivated area, water transfers, income, groundwater depletion, and the quantity and destination of water supplied to Chennai.
parsed.rationale: The “Survey” section on page 115 identifies the sample and compares selling, dependent, and non-dependent farmers under the administratively created tripartite agreement. Tables 2–4 on pages 116–118 report reduced cultivated area and water access among dependent farmers, near-elimination of local water sales, and sharply diverging incomes, while pages 113–115 quantify the purchased groundwater entering Chennai's service system. The study therefore provides empirical evidence linking a regulatory/governance arrangement to water availability and exclusion at community and utility-system levels.
